newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks close easier in lackluster dealings.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks close easier in lackluster dealings.

* Toronto's stock market ended softer on Thursday, dragged lower by weaker banks despite soaring golds. * Eye on Friday's U.S. data. * 77 million shares traded worth C$1.1 billion.

Toronto stocks eased to a lower close in light dealings on Thursday, as cautious investors hugged the sidelines ahead of Friday's U.S. economic data which may indicate whether inflation is on the rise.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index dipped 8.60 to 5790.11 in lackluster turnover of 77.3 million shares worth C$1.08 billion.
"Nothing exciting to report outside of golds," said fund manager Josef Schachter. "Golds are a little bit better."
The key gold group of Canada's largest equities market rose nearly 2.3 percent.
Despite stronger golds, heavyweight banking issues dropped more than 1.4 percent, countering the move by golds.
"Financials had a bad day," Schachter added.
Of Toronto's 14 sub-indices, eight dropped and six rose. The weak side was led by banks, conglomerates, consumer products and oils. Gainers included golds, media and base metals.
Declining issues outpaced advancers 490 to 435, while 300 traded flat.

Investors will be eyeing U.S. retail sales and producer prices for March, due out on Friday to see if the U.S. Federal Reserve will be tempted to hike short-term interest rates again when it meets again in May.
--- HOT STOCKS ---

* Closely watched Bre-X Minerals Ltd topped Toronto actives. Shares in the gold prospector jumped 0.40 to 2.67 on 14.1 million shares as investors debated the quality of its Busang gold find in Indonesia.
* Bank of Montreal, Canada's third largest, lost 1.45 to 47.20 in active dealings.
((Lydia Zajc, Reuters Toronto Bureau (416) 941-8109))
